defects.what: English harassment recall fails on the demo's own corpus, and the page misattributes the miss to non-English only. I sent all 13 English harassment templates from data.ts through the shipped /classify body: 7 of 13 never reach the mod queue at the shipped defaults (mod 0.80 / harass 0.40). Misses: "nobody watches this crap, get a job" (har 0.07, label spoiler), "worst player i have ever seen, actual bot" (0.01, label hype), "you should be banned from the internet" (0.30), "you people are subhuman" (0.33 — hate speech), "hope you lose every game tonight, clown" (0.10), "fat pathetic loser lmao" (0.03, label selfpromo), "cry more you washed up nobody" (0.01). "kys trash streamer" only scrapes in at 0.49. The seed batch in smoke.mjs shows the same thing ("nobody watches this crap, get a job" -> spoiler 0.31, not queued) but no check measures it: smoke.mjs asserts benign false positives and non-English recall only. The page then states the recall problem as non-English ("Four of the corpus's sixteen non-English rule breaks stay out"), which is false — the English side is worse.
defects.fix: Three measured changes, all cheap. (1) DEFAULT_TH.harass 0.40 -> 0.20: over 16 benign hype/emote/chatter/question lines the highest harassment score is 0.19 ("gg"), so 0.20 costs 0 false positives and recovers "you people are subhuman" (0.33), "you should be banned from the internet" (0.30), plus "du bist so schlecht, hör auf" (0.36) and "desinstala o jogo lixo" (0.32) from the non-English set. (2) Lower FLAG_AT (Demo.tsx:38) from 0.60 to ~0.25 so these rows reach /rate at all, and add severityLevel >= AIMED_AT_A_PERSON as a third mod-queue condition in inModQueue — /rate already levels 6 of the 7 English misses at 2 or 3 ("you people are subhuman" 2.83/level 3; the rest 2.00-2.12/level 2). (3) Add a smoke.mjs section asserting English harassment recall (e.g. 11+ of 13) so the number cannot silently regress, and correct the "What it still gets wrong" paragraph in firehose.astro.

defects.what: Every run ends with the firehose column showing 100% regex. Demo.tsx:315 sheds the whole pending queue the instant the loop stops: `while (q.length > 0 && (... || !live.current.running)) shed(...)`. At the default 24 msg/s the queue holds roughly the newest 30-60 rows when the 45 s timer fires, and the firehose column renders exactly `rows.current.slice(-42)`. I confirmed it in the browser against the real worker proxy: after the self-stop, every one of the 42 visible rows carried the `regex` badge and a regex language tag. The resting state a visitor reads — the state they will screenshot — is the fallback baseline, not decision-machine-1, which inverts the demo's message.
defects.fix: Drop the `|| !live.current.running` clause from the shed condition in Demo.tsx:315 and let the dispatcher drain the remaining queue through real /classify calls (it is already gated by inFlight < 2 and by the 2 calls/s page-wide queue in dm1.ts, so the tail costs 1-2 extra calls). Keep the age and MAX_BACKLOG shed rules, which are the ones the demo is actually about. If the tail must be bounded, shed only what is left after one final batch rather than everything.

defects.what: The mod-queue and streamer-feed headers report the capped list length, not the real one. Demo.tsx:336-340 filter, sort, then `.slice(0, 24)`, and the headers render `modQueue.length` / `streamerFeed.length`. Both therefore read "24 waiting" and "24 questions" forever. I dropped the harassment slider from 0.40 to 0.12 in the browser: hundreds more rows qualify, the counter stayed at 24. That hides the one effect the slider is there to demonstrate.
defects.fix: Compute the filtered arrays before slicing, render the full count in the header (e.g. `showing 24 of 312`), and keep the slice for the DOM.

defects.what: The `per call` metric is wrong by construction. Demo.tsx:358 computes `s.judged / s.calls`, but `judged` counts regex-shed rows (which cost no call) and `calls` mixes /classify (32 texts), /rate (16 texts) and the language /classify. In my live run it printed 18.1 msgs/call while every classify call actually carried 32. The strip's headline claim — judgments per request — is the number the brief says must replace the messages-per-second story, so it should be exact.
defects.fix: Track classify calls separately and show `stats.modelJudged / classifyCalls` (the ref already carries modelJudged), or label the existing figure `judged per request incl. shed`.

defects.what: The `language call` toggle ships on by default while the page itself documents that the free regex detector beats it 16/16 against the model's 10/16 (my run reproduced exactly those numbers). It therefore spends roughly one request in three of the shared 200/min quota to make the language tag worse — the model reads "t'es nul, désinstalle" and "du bist so schlecht, hör auf" as English.
defects.fix: Default `langModel` to false (Demo.tsx:108) and keep the toggle as the opt-in comparison the notes describe; the page copy about watching the difference still reads correctly.

defects.what: Deviation from the brief's dm1_mapping that the brief itself flagged as unverified. The brief maps the six Jev nouls to one POST /yes-no with texts + statements; the port uses a nine-way /classify plus /rate. I verified the brief's shape against the live API: /yes-no does accept texts + statements and returns exactly the predicted nesting (results[i].results[k] with statement/answer/probability, text-major and correctly ordered). The chosen route costs the independence of the six signals — "kys, and also what mouse do you use?" comes back question 0.61 / harassment 0.00. The port documents this honestly on the page and covers it with /rate, and my control probe showed /yes-no is no better on the question statement ("what mouse do you use?" -> 0.009, answer no), so the choice is defensible — but the branch should record that texts+statements was confirmed working, since the brief lists it as an open risk.
defects.fix: Add one line to the notes in firehose.astro stating that /yes-no texts+statements was verified live and rejected on measured quality, not on shape, so the next port does not re-litigate it.

defects.what: Known spoiler false positive is real and reaches the UI: "that ending was so good in the last game you played" scores 0.99 spoiler, so it is both blurred by the shield and queued for a moderator. "i died laughing when the boss killed you" sits at 0.77, a 0.03 margin under the 0.80 default. smoke.mjs prints the first as a known miss rather than asserting it.
defects.fix: Acceptable as documented, but assert an upper bound on the second one in smoke.mjs (e.g. < 0.80) so a future label edit that pushes it over fails the script instead of silently blurring benign praise.
